title: A finite tame cover has an etale model after a simultaneous finite root base change
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic a positive prime $p$, and let $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be a regular Noetherian separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B$, with $r\geq0$, be such that $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ is a reduced strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] and at every point $v\in V$ the $t_i$ vanishing at $v$ are part of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. The closed subschemes $V(t_i)$ need not be irreducible or connected. Set $f=\prod_i t_i$ and $V^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$, with $f=1$ when $r=0$. Let $P\to V^\circ$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, writing $A=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] and $I(\bar v)=\{i:t_i(\bar v)=0\}$, its pullback to the punctured full root tower
$$\varprojlim_{(m,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(A[z_i:i\in I(\bar v)]/(z_i^m-t_i)_{i\in I(\bar v)}\bigr)[1/\prod_{i\in I(\bar v)}t_i]$$
is a finite disjoint union of copies of that tower. Transitions are the power maps for divisibility, and $m$ ranges over positive integers prime to $p$. Then there are a positive integer $n$ prime to $p$ and a finite etale morphism $Z\to V_n$, where
$$V_n=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i\bigr),$$
together with an isomorphism of $V_n^\circ=V_n\times_V V^\circ$-schemes
$$Z\times_{V_n}V_n^\circ\simeq P\times_{V^\circ}V_n^\circ.$$
No connectedness, Galois action, invertibility of $\deg P$, henselian hypothesis, residual-cover hypothesis, or choice of roots of unity is imposed. The empty cover and $r=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1(i)–(iii) and proof, printed pp.133–134: strict-local parameter-root quotient description and etale-local descent of the finite tame normalization; finite-type-over-a-field specialization. The simultaneous finite root level is the qc consequence of the local description, not a statement about infinite coefficient objects.

proof.text: If $V=\varnothing$, $r=0$, or $P=\varnothing$, take $n=1$ and respectively $Z=\varnothing$, $P$, or $\varnothing$. Otherwise write $P=\operatorname{Spec}D$ over $B[1/f]$ and put $C_a=B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^a-t_i)_i$, $X_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$ for each positive $a$ prime to $p$. The labelled-root geometry lemma gives finite freeness over $B$, regularity and normality, injectivity of $f$, density of $X_a^\circ$ in every component, and the compatible power transitions.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed pp.133-134; finite-root normalization and etale-local descent, with the explicit finite-level assembly of the returned split.

proof.text: Put $D_a=D\otimes_{B[1/f]}C_a[1/f]$ and let $E_a$ be the integral closure of $C_a$ in $D_a$. Base change preserves etaleness; images of module generators preserve finiteness. Apply the normalization/spreading lemma with $(C,g,F)=(C_a,f,D_a)$. Thus $N_a=\operatorname{Spec}E_a$ is finite and finitely presented over $X_a$, and its canonical restriction to $X_a^\circ$ is exactly the prescribed pullback of $P$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed pp.133-134; finite-root normalization and etale-local descent, with the explicit finite-level assembly of the returned split.

proof.text: At each geometric $\bar v$ above $v$, let $A=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Apply the active-root splitting lemma to the given tower trivialization. Its hypotheses hold because $B$ is Noetherian of characteristic $p$ and all $C_a$ are normal with $f$ injective by step 1. It supplies $m_v$ prime to $p$ such that $E_{m_v}\otimes_B A\simeq(A\otimes_B C_{m_v})^d$, including $d=0$. This is a finite etale model after the actual strict-local base change, with no root-of-unity choices.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed pp.133-134; finite-root normalization and etale-local descent, with the explicit finite-level assembly of the returned split.

proof.text: For this $m_v$, the last clause of the normalization/spreading lemma applies to $N_{m_v}\to X_{m_v}$ and yields $h_v\notin v$ such that it is finite etale over $X_{m_v}\times_VW_v$, $W_v=D(h_v)$. Its punctured identification is the canonical one of step 2. Choosing a geometric point above each $v$ therefore supplies the open neighbourhoods and local covers required for common-level gluing.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed pp.133-134; finite-root normalization and etale-local descent, with the explicit finite-level assembly of the returned split.

proof.text: Apply common-level gluing to $V$, $U=V^\circ$, and the system $X_a$ with the power transitions of step 1 and the local covers of step 4. The base $V$ is quasi-compact, and every $X_a$ is normal Noetherian with componentwise dense puncture by step 1. The lemma chooses a finite subcover and $n=\prod_jm_j$, constructs unique overlap isomorphisms extending the specified puncture identifications, verifies their cocycle, and glues a finite etale $Z\to X_n$ with the required punctured isomorphism. Since $X_n=V_n$ and $n$ is positive and prime to $p$, this is the assertion.
